# PR #3775: Patch: a collection you can search: one card grid with filters and sort across the full width, and a deck builder that drags by touch and splits on an upright iPad

Closes #3734

## What changed

**The Collection** (`R3734000`, amends `R1579000`). `/collection` now fills the window as four tabs: Cards, Decks, Cosmetics and Progress. They are switched by `?section=`, and an unknown or missing name opens Cards. The route holds each tab's search, filters and sort, so they survive a switch.
- **Cards** is one virtual grid of every collectible card (`CardGrid.tsx`).
  - It reuses the deck builder pool's windowing (`poolWindow.ts`, `usePoolWindow`) and its search, filter and sort code (`filters.ts`, `FilterBar.tsx`).
  - Filters are cost, set, type, rarity, keyword and All, Owned or Missing.
  - Sorts are cost, name, rarity, **Set** and **Newest**. Set and Newest are new, and the deck builder and the Almanac get them too.
  - The search and sort are a toolbar that is always on screen. The chip rows are a sidebar over 1024px and a sheet under it (`BrowsePanel.tsx`).
  - The page also shows an owned count (`312 / 480`) and a `<progress>` for each set.
- **Progress** holds the wallet, set tracks, Fleet track and quests, moved out from under the card list.
- **Decks** are tiles showing portrait, name, validity and modes (Best of 1, Conquest, or "Not playable yet"), both from the validator's verdicts. A tile links to `/decks?deck=<id>`, which opens that deck. The workshop's Back now returns to this tab.
- **Cosmetics** gets the same search, rarity chips, owned or missing view and sort; its previews are unchanged.

**The deck builder** (`R3734001`, amends `R3728000`).
- `DeckDrag.tsx` drags a pool card to the deck with pointer events. The HTML5 drag and drop is removed.
- A touch lifts a card only when it moves across. `touch-action: pan-y` leaves a vertical start to scroll.
- A release outside the deck, Escape, a cancel or a blur adds nothing.
- The rail, pool and deck sit side by side from 601px. The workshop's rail is 148px from 601 to 1024px, and the list and editor take turns only at 600px and under.
- The 1277px exception is gone from `breakpoints.test.ts`.

## How I tested it
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project web --changed origin/main …` (the harness command): 385 of 386 files passed. The failure was `navigation-reads.test.tsx` timing out at 5s drawing the full catalog in jsdom. I mocked `COLLECTED_DEFS` to 48 cards there, as in `routes/collection.test.tsx`, and it passes. I did not re-run the whole set after that fix.
- Vitest on the plan's sets plus `navigation-reads.test.tsx`: 768 tests passed. That includes the CSS budget tests, with the collection sheet counts lowered and the new `browse.css` on tokens only.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, the e2e typechecks, `pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e` and `cargo jackioh spec check` are clean.
- Cypress component specs in Electron: `collection-screen` (25 passing, at 360×740, 390×844, 820×1180, 1180×820 and 1280×800), `deckbuilder-touch-drag` (5 passing, touch events at 820×1180) and `deckbuilder-layout` (21 of 24 passing).
- **Red in `deckbuilder-layout`:** three `fitEveryPoolCard` tests time out at 60s (rules text at least 9px, twice, and keywords in bold). I ran the same spec on `main` at `3867182459` in a worktree and the same three fail there.
- **Not run here:**
  - e2e specs 45, 46 and 47 are edited and typecheck, but need the server and database, so they ran in neither the harness's checks nor mine.
  - No Rust changed, so cargo fmt, clippy and test were not run.
- **Screenshots:** I could not attach them from this run. I looked at Cypress screenshots at 390, 820 and 1280 myself, which is how I found and fixed the tab bar shrinking to zero height under the Cards grid.

## Decisions the issue did not settle
All of these are in the ruling notes with the alternatives I rejected.
- Progress is a fourth tab, not a strip, because a strip would eat the grid's height.
- The cost row stays 0 to 5, 6+, X, the shared `COST_BUCKETS`, because 0 to 7+ would change the mana curve and saved filters.
- Type chips are the deck builder's five, not Unit, Spell and Trap.
- Newest means the latest patch in `PATCH_LOG`.
- A touch lifts on a move across, not on press-and-hold, which would collide with the preview hold.
- The workshop rail narrows to 148px between 601 and 1024px, not a bottom deck tray.
- The Collection's sort select offers the issue's five sorts only. The deck builder's bar keeps all nine.

## Departures from the plan
- `FilterBar` takes `part: "toolbar" | "chips"` instead of `stacked`, so the search stays visible when the chips are in a sheet. It also takes a `sorts` prop.

- `DeckDrag` takes an optional `nameOf` prop for the ghost text and calls `preventDefault` on `touchmove` while a card is in flight.
- The Cosmetics sort has a third key, "registry" (the default order).
- The "New deck" tile at the deck limit is a disabled button.
- The sidebar is 260px wide so the grid is wider than 960px at 1280.

It made Cypress fail on "ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications" when a sidebar changed the grid's width. Window resizes still flush synchronously. # #3734: Patch: a collection you can search: one card grid with filters and sort across the full width, and a deck builder that drags by touch and splits on an upright iPad
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

### What it does

The collection becomes a place to browse and find cards, as the Hearthstone, Marvel Snap and LoR collections are. It gets one grid with a search box, filters and sort, uses the whole window, and puts the filters in a sidebar on a wide screen. The deck builder works with a finger, and shows the pool and the deck side by side on an upright iPad.

It follows the conventions in #3728's `docs/polish/10-menus.md`.

### Where it stands

- **The Collection** (`routes/collection.tsx`, `collection/*`, `collection/collection.css`):
  - It sits in the account page's `panel--auth` frame, at most 960px wide.
  - Its hub is three doors: Decks, Cards and Cosmetics.
  - **Cards** is an accordion with one set open at a time (`collection/OwnedCards.tsx`). It has no search, filter or sort, and no virtualisation. The wallet, the tracks, the Fleet track and the quests sit below it.
  - **Cosmetics** is a Board and Starship tab pair (`AccountCosmeticTiles`, `StarshipLooks`). A card opens `CardCosmeticsView`, `ItemPreview` (on a hold), `LookHover` and `LooksScreen`.
- **The deck builder** (`game/deckbuilder/`, `DeckWorkshop.tsx`):
  - Its pool already has search, filters and virtualisation.
  - The list rail sits beside the editor only from 1101px (`WORKSHOP_SPLIT_MIN_WIDTH_PX`). Below that the two take turns, so an upright iPad (820 wide) shows half a builder at a time.
  - The pool drags with HTML5 `draggable` (`PoolGrid.tsx:250`), which never fires on touch. Only tap to add works on an iPad.

### What changes

- **Full width, tabs.** The Collection leaves the 960px frame and fills the window. The three doors become tabs (Cards, Decks, Cosmetics) that keep their filters while you switch. `?section=` keeps working.
- **Cards**:
  - One grid of the whole catalog, with a search box that is always visible.
  - Filter chips: cost (a row from 0 to 7+, as Hearthstone's mana row), set, type (Unit, Spell, Trap), rarity, owned or missing, and keyword.
  - Sort by cost, name, rarity, set or newest.
  - The owned count ("312 / 480") and a progress bar for each set.
  - The deck builder pool's search, filter and virtualisation code is reused, not written again.
  - Filters sit in a left sidebar at the wide width and in a sheet below it.
  - The grid's columns fit the width.
  - Under the one-screen rule (`one-screen` in `index.css`), the grid scrolls inside the screen.
- **Progress.** The wallet, tracks, Fleet track and quests move out from under the card list into a Progress strip or tab of their own.
- **Cosmetics** uses the same grid, search and filters. Its previews (hold to preview #2730, hover #3016) stay.
- **Decks** are tiles showing the hero portrait, the deck's name, its validity and the modes it can play.
- **The deck builder**:
  - Dragging from the pool to the deck uses pointer events, so a finger works. The board's `game/drag/` is the model.
  - The pool and the deck sit side by side from the medium width (an upright iPad), with a narrower rail or a deck tray along the bottom. The 1101px split's exception leaves `breakpoints.test.ts`.

### Acceptance

- Search, each filter and each sort narrow or order the grid correctly. Unit tests cover the filter and sort logic, which is shared with the deck builder's pool.
- The grid stays smooth with the whole catalog. It is virtualised as the pool is, with a test that a few hundred cards render only what is on screen.
- A deck can be built by touch drag alone. A Cypress spec drags with touch events at an iPad size.
- At 820×1180 the deck builder shows the pool and the deck at once (the `deckbuilder-layout` component spec).
- The collection tests (`routes/collection.test.*`, `collection/collection.test.tsx`), the `collection-screen` and `deckbuilder-layout` component specs and the e2e specs on these screens (45 among them) move to the new layout.
- Screenshots at the tracker's device sizes (#3728) in the pull request.
- Every required check is green.

Blocked by #3728. Part of #3726.
